chunks: Abu ʿAli al-Ashʿari, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-ʿAlaʾ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:

I asked him about a child who steals. He said: “If he steals once while he is young, he is pardoned. If he repeats it, the tips of his fingers are cut. If he repeats it, lower than his fingertips is cut. If he repeats it, lower than that is cut.”

key_terms.أَسْفَلُ: lower than, meaning a lower part of the hand than what was previously cut
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: a young boy or minor child
key_terms.عُفِيَ: was pardoned and not punished for the offense

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child who steals repeatedly in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a minor who commits theft repeatedly. It indicates an escalating disciplinary response, beginning with pardon for the first offense in childhood and followed by progressively harsher corporal penalties upon repetition.
